speaker: Danny Cole
greetingFirst: Morning, Chief. Well, I wouldn't call it morning, exactly. You can't see the sun for all this dust. Remember: the storm lifts around half past five, and then everyone flies out. We've got until 5:30 to crack this.
greetings: Chief. The coffee's terrible, but at least it's hot.
There you are, Chief. Anything you need?
Chief. The wind's taken another shingle off the roof. What can I do for you?
Back again, Chief? I've been staring at that board so long it's starting to stare back.
walkieOpen: I hear you, Chief. Mostly. This storm's chewing up the signal.

menu.people: Tell me about the people here.

situation: Here's where we stand, Chief. Cornelius Pryce, the man who owns this airfield, was found dead this morning, locked inside his office in the hangar.
Nobody can leave. The dust storm has grounded every plane, and the road's buried. It should clear around half past five this evening.
When it does, everyone flies home, including whoever killed him. So we've got until then to work out who did it, how they did it, and why.
situationLater: We've still got until about half past five, Chief. Every bit of evidence you find goes up on the board here, and you can read everything we've got in the case file. Press J for it anytime.
peopleIntro: Who do you want to know about?

people.pryce: Cornelius Pryce. Sixty-two. He built Pryce Transcontinental Air from nothing. Charming, loved a big show, and used to getting his own way. He's the one who's dead.
people.vivienne: Vivienne Pryce, his wife. Used to be an actress on the stage. Very elegant, very sharp tongue. She calls everybody 'darling', and I don't think she means it.
people.billie: Captain Billie Strand, the company's pilot. Loud, funny, a bit superstitious. She has burn scars on her hands, and she clams up if you mention the Marigold.
people.lindqvist: Doctor Lindqvist, Pryce's physician. Gentle, nervous, very careful. His hands shake. He's the one who examined the body this morning.
people.julian: Julian Ferreira-Blake. He's from Meridian Air, the rival airline. Smooth, very polite, never raises his voice. He hums opera when he thinks no one's listening.
people.ox: Abel Brennan, but everyone calls him Ox. The mechanic. Huge fellow, but gentle, slow to speak, goes to church. Keeps pigeons. I'd bet he's a terrible liar.
people.tamsin: Tamsin Quill, Pryce's secretary. Blunt, smokes like a chimney, and says straight out that she hated him. Either very honest or very clever.
people.hobbs: Walter Hobbs runs the radio. Old fellow, kind, a bit hard of hearing, and he wanders off the subject. He thinks the radio wires are haunted. He met us at the hangar last night.

nextNone: Right now? Get to know the place, Chief. Walk around, see who's where, and come back here when you've found something. Anything you find goes on the board.
Have a look around the airfield and talk to people when they're about. The reports on my desk will fill in some background as the day goes on.
hintIntro: Here's how I see it, Chief.
If it were my case, which, thank God, it isn't...
hintMore: Want me to spell it out a bit more? It'll cost us a few more minutes.
hintMaxed: That's everything I've got on that one, Chief. The rest is up to you.
hintNone: Honestly? I think we've done all we can for now.
reportsNew: There's {n} new on the desk, Chief. Typed up nice and neat. Don't spill anything on them.
reportsNone: Nothing new yet. I'll keep the wire warm.
stay: I'll wait right here. I won't wander off.
home: Back to the shed, then. I'll keep the stove going.
radioFollow: On my way, Chief. Give me a minute to find you in this soup.

reminders.15:00: Chief, it's three o'clock. Storm's due to lift around half past five. Then everybody flies home, including whoever did this.
reminders.16:30: One hour left, Chief. If we're going to file a theory, now's the time.

reactions.C01: Chief, that's not a heart-attack face.
reactions.C03: Bolted from inside. So how did anybody get out?
reactions.C04: A kid's music box? In his office?
reactions.C08: Zürich at five in the morning. Two passengers. Who was the second one?
reactions.C21: So it wasn't Pryce who sent for us. Then who did?
reactions.C25: Small hands. Scarred. Nobody at that dinner has hands like that.
reactions.C27: Six on the manifest, five certificates... Chief, that's not a clerical error.
reactions.default: Pinning it up on the board, Chief.
reactions.F01: Bolted from the inside, Chief. So how did anybody get out?
reactions.F02: A way in through the floor. That changes everything.
reactions.F03: Twenty to ten, give or take. So he was dead before that music box ever played.
reactions.F04: Chief, that's not a heart-attack face. Somebody poisoned him.
reactions.F05: Cyanide in the decanter. Anyone who could get into that room could have done it.
reactions.F07: Somebody wound that music box after he was dead. Who, and why?
reactions.F09: So the 'gunshot' was an engine. One less thing to chase.
reactions.F21: Zürich at five in the morning. Two passengers. Who was the second one?
reactions.F22: He was going to confess. That's a motive for half the people at that dinner.
reactions.F27: Miss Quill was squeezing him. That's ugly, Chief, but blackmailers want their mark alive.

rest: Get some rest, Chief. I'll wake you in half an hour.
typewriter: Not yet, Chief. When we've got the who, the how, the where and the why, I'll type it up and we'll file it.
lab: That's the fingerprint kit, Chief: powder, brushes and the good magnifying glass. Bring me something to dust.
timelineEmpty: We'll need some hard facts before we can pin the night down. Right now it's all 'about nine-ish'.
wake: Rise and shine, Chief. Half an hour, like I promised.

solved.S1: Every way out checked and on film. Only the floor's left, Chief.
solved.S2: Pink skin and bitter almonds. I read about that in a manual once. Cyanide.
solved.S3: So the music box was playing after he died. That gives me goosebumps, Chief.
solved.S4: Prussian blue. That's cyanide, all right. In the decanter.
solved.S5: Four papers in one safe, and nearly every one is somebody's secret. He kept everyone on a leash, didn't he?
solved.S6: A trapdoor. Chief, there's something under this airfield.

startRadio: Chief, it's Danny. Nobody can leave Sable Flat: the dust storm has every plane grounded until about half past five this evening. When it lifts, everyone flies home, including whoever killed Pryce. So we've got until 5:30 to solve this. Press R if you need me.

startChoices.tips: Any tips before I start, Danny?

tipsIntro: Sure, Chief. What do you want to know?
tipsDone: Good luck, Chief. Press R any time if you need me, and ask me to remind you how things work.

tipsList.label: How do I look around?
lines: Walk up to anything that catches your eye and press E to look at it, pick it up or open it. When you're aiming at something you can use, a little prompt tells you what E will do, and how many minutes it takes.
Tab opens your notebook: your leads, what you've noticed, and your own notes. You can write in it any time. J is the case file, M is the map, F is your flashlight.

tipsList.label: How do the investigations work?
lines: The big pieces of work are numbered, S1 to S26. We do them in order: one only opens when every one before it is solved. If you open one too early, I'll tell you what's still left.
Stuck? Radio me and ask 'What should I do next?'. Each hint costs five minutes, and the third one practically gives it away.

One exception: S21, the stakeout, only works at dusk, half past four, so the ones after it don't wait for it. At the very end you file your theory at the typewriter here at HQ (S26). Nobody goes down any trapdoors before that.

tipsList.label: How do I get people to talk?
lines: Walk up to someone and press E. Ask about the topics they offer, show them something you found, or watch them closely for a tell.
Every one of them has a trust level: you'll see it next to their name. It starts at 50. Friendly questions raise it, and so does showing them the right evidence. Pressing them hard lowers it.
Some things they'll only tell you once they trust you. Ask too early and they'll say 'not yet', and it costs you a little trust. Be kind first, then come back and ask again.

tipsList.label: What counts as evidence?
lines: One clue on its own is only a lead. A finding counts once you've got enough separate sources for it: something you found, a puzzle you solved, what somebody told you. Most need two or three.
Your notebook shows each lead and how many sources it has. Once a finding is proven, it goes up on the board here at HQ. Your theory at the end can only use proven findings.

tipsList.label: What about the time?
lines: The clock's in the corner. Everything takes time: looking at things, asking questions, puzzles, even walking. About a minute for every forty metres.
Calling me on the radio costs five minutes unless I'm standing next to you. If you're worn out, the cot here at HQ gives you half an hour's rest.
I'll radio at three and at half past four. At half past five the storm lifts and everyone flies home. If we haven't solved it by then, it goes cold.

tipsList.label: Does the game save?
lines: It saves itself all the time, Chief: after everything you do, and when you close it. Come back whenever you like and you'll pick up right where you left off.
